explanation.summary: Each year, hundreds of thousands of Americans move between states. This chart shows the net flow on four well-known routes: the number who moved one way minus the number who moved back. All four routes run from expensive states to cheaper, warmer ones, and all four surged during the pandemic.
explanation.methodology: State-to-state migration tables from the Census Bureau's American Community Survey (1-year estimates, people aged 1 and over who lived in a different state a year earlier), 2005-2024. Net flow = people moving from A to B minus people moving from B to A. 2020 was not published, so 2019-2021 is a straight line. Each estimate has a margin of error of several thousand people.

key_findings.title: 2012: Moving Slows Down
key_findings.description: After the housing crash, few people could sell their homes and move. Net moves from California to Arizona fell to about 6,000, from 66,000 in 2005.
key_findings.significance: When home prices fall, people get stuck in place.

key_findings.title: 2021-2022: The Pandemic Move
key_findings.description: With remote work, net moves from California to Texas reached about 74,000 in 2021 and from New York to Florida about 70,000 in 2022.
key_findings.significance: Remote work let people keep big-city jobs while living somewhere cheaper.

key_findings.title: 2024: The Wave Cools
key_findings.description: Net moves fell sharply: California to Texas about 32,000 (77,000 moved there, 45,000 moved back) and New York to Florida about 23,000.
key_findings.significance: Higher home prices and insurance costs in Texas and Florida slowed the flow.
